boundary_rationale: Onset: the word-event formula opens the part and the parent, Ezek.33.1 “וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר” — one of the book's 39 strict word-event onsets and a hard seam; it also carries the parent seam named in the binding strategy (P6/P7), since the addressee returns from the nations to “the children of your people” in the next verse, Ezek.33.2 “בֶּן אָדָ֗ם דַּבֵּ֤ר אֶל בְּנֵֽי עַמְּךָ֙ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם אֶ֕רֶץ כִּֽי אָבִ֥יא עָלֶ֖יהָ חָ֑רֶב וְלָקְח֨וּ עַם הָאָ֜רֶץ אִ֤ישׁ אֶחָד֙ מִקְצֵיהֶ֔ם וְנָתְנ֥וּ אֹת֛וֹ לָהֶ֖ם לְצֹפֶֽה”. Close: the row ends where the watchman analogy itself ends, at Ezek.33.9 “וְ֠אַתָּה כִּֽי הִזְהַ֨רְתָּ רָשָׁ֤ע מִדַּרְכּוֹ֙ לָשׁ֣וּב מִמֶּ֔נָּה וְלֹא שָׁ֖ב מִדַּרְכּ֑וֹ ה֚וּא בַּעֲוֺנ֣וֹ יָמ֔וּת וְאַתָּ֖ה נַפְשְׁךָ֥ הִצַּֽלְתָּ”, corroborated by a samekh mark following that verse (single-witness, disclosed). No recognition or utterance refrain closes this sub-unit — the close is topical, not formulaic, and is disclosed as such rather than claimed as a formula match. Both sides weighed: onset side carries the hard-seam word-event plus the addressee return; close side carries the samekh mark plus the topical shift at Ezek.33.10, where “son of man” reopens with a distinct target (“the house of Israel”) and a quoted popular saying, the disputation-oracle device that opens the next row.

An oath-plus-utterance combination follows at Ezek.33.11 “אֱמֹ֨ר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם חַי אָ֣נִי נְאֻ֣ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה אִם אֶחְפֹּץ֙ בְּמ֣וֹת הָרָשָׁ֔ע כִּ֣י אִם בְּשׁ֥וּב רָשָׁ֛ע מִדַּרְכּ֖וֹ וְחָיָ֑ה שׁ֣וּבוּ שׁ֜וּבוּ מִדַּרְכֵיכֶ֧ם הָרָעִ֛ים וְלָ֥מָּה תָמ֖וּתוּ בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל”, carrying its own pe mark; this is disclosed as close-grade material that is NOT final here, because the same disputation continues through a second “son of man” sub-onset at Ezek.33.12 restating the principle for “the children of your people” and on through the righteous/wicked case-pairs of 33.14-19. Close: a second pe mark follows Ezek.33.20 “וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֕ם לֹ֥א יִתָּכֵ֖ן דֶּ֣רֶךְ אֲדֹנָ֑י אִ֧ישׁ כִּדְרָכָ֛יו אֶשְׁפּ֥וֹט אֶתְכֶ֖ם בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל”, which restates the people's complaint and YHWH's verdict (“I will judge every one of you after his ways”) verbatim against 33.17, marking the disputation's true end. MT 33.20 carries NO sof-pasuq in this witness — it stands instead with an untyped OSHB editorial note, “We read punctuation in L differently from BHS,” immediately before the pe. This is disclosed as a single-witness punctuation divergence; no boundary is argued from the absent mark, only from the pe that follows and the topical restatement it closes.

boundary_rationale: Onset: the dateline at Ezek.33.21 “וַיְהִ֞י בִּשְׁתֵּ֧י עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֗ה בָּעֲשִׂרִ֛י בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֥ה לַחֹ֖דֶשׁ לְגָלוּתֵ֑נוּ בָּא אֵלַ֨י הַפָּלִ֧יט מִירוּשָׁלִַ֛ם לֵאמֹ֖ר הֻכְּתָ֥ה הָעִֽיר” — one of the book's 14 year-bearing oracle datelines and a hard seam — reports the fugitive's arrival with news the city has fallen. This hand-of-YHWH occurrence opens no vision here — it is narrative notice, not a scene-transport marker. Close: a pe mark follows Ezek.33.22 (single-witness), and the verse completes the narrative beat before Ezek.33.23 opens a fresh, formally distinct word-event oracle.
